cost.note: translation is parse+elaborate+emit, linear in the program; reducer-generated 50KB tasks take ~2s

notes: The first cross-language pair of Era 6, carried over from Era 5 with its channels made explicit. prog (T.py): a c program as a bit-vector machine — T embeds the c interpreter's own front end verbatim and encodes the elaborated CFG it executes: one btor2 state for the program counter and for every slot (arrays as btor2 array states, broadcast-0 init, bounds-guarded reads/writes mirroring the interpreter's out-of-range rule), one btor2 input per havoc site in site order, absorbing HALT/ERR codes past the locations, bad = (pc == ERR). Every CFG node is one transition, so bad AND depth carry exactly and a universal claim at btor2 bound k is a bound-k fact at the C level — no bound_cap, so claim crosses back at the full bound. obs: both languages name the observables identically, maps is the identity. wit (lam_wit.py): re-runs the builder to reproduce the site-to-input-node map (a pure function of the program) and carries a btor2 stimulus back as a renaming; corpus 002 exercises it with three inputs of three widths, and the two wit mutants (values dropped, frames shifted) fail there. cert (lam_cert.py, revision 2 — the canonical (b)-move): a btor2 certificate carried back as a C-level one by re-running the builder for its state map: k-induction passes through (frames align, one node per transition), bit-invariants and clause invariants are renamed from btor2 state bits to machine atoms (pc bits, slot bits) and re-discharged by c@2's own judge; three corpus certificates round-trip and three cert mutants fail. Out of the pair's fragment: nonzero global array initializers. Pre-admission evidence (Era 5): the square held on 1188 of 1188 random dual-keyed stimulus runs across all 594 in-fragment SV-COMP tasks.
